lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: why the whole must always be identified
lessonRef.title: Applied problem solving: why the whole must always be identified

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the problem below asks for.

items.prompt: A shape is divided into 6 equal parts. 5 are shaded. What fraction is shaded?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what the problem is asking before you compute.

items.prompt: A shape is divided into 6 equal parts. 5 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?
A shape is divided into 4 equal parts. 1 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A shape is divided into 6 equal parts. 4 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?
A shape is divided into 8 equal parts. 4 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?
A shape is divided into 8 equal parts. 5 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: A shape is divided into 6 equal parts. 2 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A shape is divided into 8 equal parts. 3 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
